title: Apollo 13 - CSM Odyssey, LM Aquarius
_comment: Apollo 13, the LM as a lifeboat: cryogenic oxygen tank 2 in the service module failed at 55:54:53 on the way out, and Aquarius, docked, powered and flew the stack from then to the entry: its descent engine put it back on a free return and, two hours past the Moon, sped the return up and moved it to the Pacific; its crew flew the last corrections on its abort guidance system and its jets, jettisoned the service module, powered the command module up again and left Aquarius an hour before the entry. Its launch flew on with the S-II's centre engine shut down by pogo 132 s early, the IU's guidance burning the other four and the S-IVB longer to the parking orbit. Sources: the Apollo 13 Mission Report (MSC-02680) and its guidance supplement, the Saturn V flight evaluation report for AS-508 (MPR-SAT-FE-70-2), the AS-508 postflight trajectory (D5-15560-8), and the Apollo Flight Journal's transcripts. Distances in km, times in GET seconds or hhh:mm:ss (GET counts from range zero, 19:13:00 UTC on 11 April 1970).

call_signs._comment: The call signs CAPCOM used for the flight and its vehicles (Apollo Flight Journal) [published]; CAPCOM's own calls on the timeline say 13, Odyssey and Aquarius where he did

start_calls.launch: T minus 25 seconds and counting and Apollo 13 is Go. T minus 20 seconds and counting.
start_calls.translunar_coast: {mission}, Houston. Good TLI. MCC-2 will take you off the free return, 60 miles over the Moon.
start_calls.tank_failure: 13, we've got one more item for you, when you get a chance. We'd like you to stir up your cryo tanks.
start_calls._comment: CAPCOM's word as each start phase begins, the simulator's own [adapted]; at the launch's, the launch commentator's count (Apollo Flight Journal) [published]; at tank_failure's, Jack Lousma's at 55:52:58, a minute before the tank failed (Apollo Flight Journal) [published]

vehicles._comment: Apollo 13's vehicles where they differ from data/spacecraft.json's, Apollo 11's

mass._source: The mission report's mass properties (MSC-02680, Table A-I: the CSM 63,720.3 lb and the LM 33,499.1 lb at transposition and docking, the stack 96,038.7 lb after the oxygen tank incident, the CM 12,367.6 lb after its separation from the LM) and propellant loads (section 7: the SPS's 40,769 lb, 40,529.7 lb of it left at the incident; the SM RCS's 1,342.8 lb; the CM RCS's 245.1 lb; the DPS's 18,434.5 lb; the LM RCS's 633.0 lb) [published]. From them [derived]: the CM dry of its RCS's propellant; the SM dry of its own propellant and the SPS's at the incident, which leaves out the oxygen the incident lost and what the flight had used before it, so that the stack weighs what it weighed from the incident on [simplified: the SM RCS's load full then, and the stack 941 lb light at the docking]; the LM's stages, the LM at docking less its loads, split by Apollo 12's descent stage dry and Apollo 11's ascent engine load [estimated: Aquarius's ascent engine never fired]; the S-IVB dry with the Instrument Unit, the adapter and the residuals, AS-507's (Apollo 12's) [estimated]

sps._source: The SPS's load, 40,769 lb (MSC-02680, section 7.1.1) [published]; its engine Apollo 11's

sm_rcs._source: The SM RCS's load, 1,342.8 lb in four quads (MSC-02680, section 7.1.2) [published]

cm_rcs._source: The CM RCS's load, 122.0 and 123.1 lb in its two systems (MSC-02680, section 7.1.2) [published]

dps._source: The DPS's load, 18,434.5 lb (MSC-02680, section 7.2.1) [published]; its engine Apollo 11's

lm_rcs._source: The LM RCS's load, 316.5 lb in each of its two systems (MSC-02680, section 7.2.2) [published]

sivb._source: The J-2 in AS-508's second S-IVB burn, TLI: 350.8 s from the second ignition, the stage's propellant 161,922 lbm (73,447 kg) at it and 6,079 lbm at the cutoff signal (MPR-SAT-FE-70-2, sections 7.8 and 7.9, Table 7-3's best estimates), its specific impulse at the steady-state slice, 427.2 s (Table 7-2) [published]; the thrust the burn's mean flow gives at that specific impulse [derived; the thrust and the specific impulse held through the burn, where the J-2 ran its first 100 s at a lower mixture ratio (ibid., Figure 7-7): simplified]

lm_eps._source: Aquarius's batteries at their power-up, 2,179 A-h (MSC-02680, section 7.2.5) [published]

s_ic._source: AS-508's F-1s: 6,725.7 kN and an Isp of 265.0 s each reduced to sea level, the five engines' average at the 35 to 38 s time slice (MPR-SAT-FE-70-2, Table 5-1) [published, averaged: derived]; 7,836 kN each in vacuum at OECO, the peak 37.60 m/s2 on 833,627 kg over four engines (ibid., Tables 4-1 and 16-9) [derived], the exit area the difference over the sea level's pressure [derived]; the propellant the vehicle's mass from holddown release to OECO (ibid., Table 16-9) [derived], the vacuum Isp that burns it by the flown OECO, 163.60 s [estimated]

s_ii._source: AS-508's second flight stage at the S-II's start command, its aft interstage and launch escape system jettisoned, and 212,921 kg at its cutoff signal (MPR-SAT-FE-70-2, Table 16-9) [published], the propellant between them [derived]; five J-2s at the high mixture ratio, 5,163.3 kN 62 s after the start command (ibid., section 6.3 and Table 6-1), and 3,067.0 kN on the four outboard engines at the low ratio after the shift (ibid.) [published]; the low ratio's flow at the 427 s Isp read off the report's Figure 6-3, and the high ratio's the flow that burns the rest by the flown cutoff, 592.64 s [estimated]

s_ivb._source: AS-508's third flight stage at the S-IVB's first start command (MPR-SAT-FE-70-2, Table 16-9); the J-2 in the first burn, 199,577 lbf on 176.03 kg/s of LOX and 35.86 kg/s of LH2 (ibid., Table 7-1) [published]

saturn_v._source: AS-508, Apollo 13's Saturn V, where it differs from spacecraft.json's AS-506: at holddown arm release 2,909,779 kg (MPR-SAT-FE-70-2, Table 16-9) [published]; its drag and its guidance failure's rate AS-506's [estimated]

calls.liftoff: We have commit and we have lift-off - at 2:13.

launch._comment: Apollo 13's launch from Launch Complex 39A at 19:13:00 UTC on 11 April 1970, GET 0, on AS-508 [published]. The pad's coordinates are Apollo 11's, taken as geocentric [simplified]. The start phase begins on the pad at start_get_s: guidance reference release at grr_get_s, the S-IC's start sequence commanded at ignition_get_s, all engines running by thrust_ok_get_s, the holddown arms' release at release_get_s and T1 at t1_get_s (Saturn V launch vehicle flight evaluation report, AS-508, MPR-SAT-FE-70-2, Tables 2-1 and 2-2) [published]. The Instrument Unit's boost program on its time bases as AS-508 flew it (ibid.) [published]: the roll and pitch program at 12.6 s, the S-IC's centre engine cutoff (135.18 s) on T1, the tilt arrest (163.3 s) on T2; T3 at the outboard engines' cutoff (163.60 s), which the propellant ends, then staging, the S-II's start, its aft interstage's separation, the launch escape tower's jettison, the iterative guidance's start, and the S-II's centre engine cutoff the IU still commanded on T3 at 462.6 s, 132 s after pogo had shut the engine down (the mission's failures); the shift to the low mixture ratio on the IU's velocity criterion, its command 'upon attainment of a preprogramed velocity increase as sensed by the LVDC' (ibid., section 6.5) at 534.7 s, 32.2 s later than predicted, the engines shifting 2.8 s later (emr_delay_s), emr_dv_mps the sensed velocity gain since the S-II's start command that brings the command at the flown time [derived: the simulator's own flight]; T4 at the S-II's cutoff (592.64 s), then staging and the S-IVB's ignition; T5 at the S-IVB's velocity cutoff (749.83 s), and insertion 10 s after it (759.83 s). The yaw away from the tower, the attitude rate limit and the time-tilt pitch polynomial are SA-504's presettings, as Apollo 11's [estimated for AS-508, whose presettings aren't at hand], toward the flight azimuth, 72.043 deg (ibid., section 4.1) [published]. The S-IVB loses parking_orbit_loss_kg between its first burn's end and its second start command: 134,408 kg and 133,479 kg (ibid., Table 16-9) [derived]; the simulator takes it off at insertion [simplified]. The calls are the flight's (Apollo Flight Journal, Apollo 13, launch and ascent to Earth orbit): the launch commentator's and Lovell's [published]

calls: We confirm skirt SEP. Roger. Tower Jett; mode II, Jim. Looking good.
13, Houston. Stand by for S-IVB to COI capability.
Roger. You've got it now, Jim.
Jim, Houston. We don't have a story on why the inboard out was early, but the other engines are Go and you are Go.
13, Houston. Level sense arm time, 8 plus 38 nominal; S-II cut-off time, 9 plus 48. Over.
Mark. You have S-IVB to orbit, Jim.
Mark. You have mode IV, Jim.
13, Houston. At 11 minutes, you're Go. Predicted cut-off on the S-IVB is 12 plus 34. Over.
launch_aborts._comment: Apollo 13's launch abort modes, Apollo 11's (its mission.json's launch_aborts) on the same vehicles [estimated], at the times Houston marked them on Apollo 13's flight (Apollo Flight Journal, Apollo 13, launch and ascent to Earth orbit) [published]: Mode I Bravo at 0:42, Mode I Charlie at 1:58, mode II after the tower's jettison at 3:21, S-IVB to COI capability at 5:48, S-IVB to orbit at 7:11 and Mode IV at 9:48. Mode III from 8 s before the S-II's cutoff, as Apollo 11's came [estimated: Houston didn't call it]. The calls are Kerwin's, with his word on the centre engine as it came [published]

parking_orbit._comment: Apollo 13's orbit at insertion, from the AS-508 postflight trajectory (D5-15560-8, Table 4-III): inclination 32.525 deg and descending node 123.084 deg east of the launch meridian at range zero, insertion at 759.83 s at 32.694 N 50.490 W, 191.6 km up [published], put in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. The report's 185.7 x 183.9 km orbit is taken as circular [simplified]. The launch start (slice 10d) flies to it on AS-508's stages (vehicles saturn_v, launch)

launch_refsmmat._comment: The launch pad REFSMMAT, the orientation the CMC's IMU was released at liftoff: X horizontal along the flight azimuth (72.043 deg, D5-15560-8, section 4), Z down along Launch Complex 39A's vertical, Y = Z x X, each a stable member axis in the ICRF, from tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. The parking_orbit and translunar_coast start phases start aligned to it

tli._comment: TLI's conic, as the flown TLI left the stack on it: C3 -1,376,274 m2/s2 and eccentricity 0.9772, in the plane of inclination 31.817 deg and descending node 122.997 deg (D5-15560-8, Table 4-IV: at TLI, 10 s after the cutoff signal) [published]; the plane in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]; the TLI perigee's place in the burn, which starts it at the flown 2:35:46.4 [derived]. TLI left the stack on a free return past the Moon 86.8 nmi up at 77:56:22 (MSC-02680, Table 4-III) [published], and the transposition and docking's thrusting moved that to 250.2 nmi at 77:46:46, where the report's state at the first midcourse correction's ignition (ibid., Table 4-II) passes the Moon in the simulator [derived: with the cutoff's latitude, 22.80 N; the ignition's 22.93 N is 500 km from it 3.5 s earlier]. The RTCC plans TLI's ignition time and energy (Rtcc.plan_tli()) for that trajectory, aim_pericynthion [simplified: the transposition and docking's thrusting isn't flown]. The midcourse correction then aims at pericynthion_alt_km at pericynthion_get, the PAD's 60 nmi (Apollo Flight Journal, 028:53:25) at the flown 77:28:39 (63 nmi, MSC-02680, Table 4-III) [published], in the hybrid trajectory's plane there (lunar_site): off the free return, for LOI into the orbit over Fra Mauro. earliest_get_s: 2:10:00, ahead of the S-IVB's restart preparation, time base 6 at 2:26:08.1 (Apollo Flight Journal) [estimated]

lunar_site._comment: Without a lunar orbit, the plane the midcourse correction puts the pericynthion in is the hybrid trajectory's, through the pericynthion it left: 3.34 N 178.93 E at 77:28:39 (MSC-02680, Table 4-III) [published], heading 274.6 deg there, as the report's state at the correction's cutoff (ibid., Table 4-II) passes the Moon in the simulator: 64.1 nmi at 77:28:41, 3.72 N 178.99 E [derived]

tank_failure._comment: The tank_failure start phase: five minutes before cryogenic oxygen tank 2 failed, at 55:54:53 (MSC-02680, Table 3-I) [published], TLI and the translunar midcourse correction the timeline had flown by then (mcc: its entries) flown on the SPS. The CMC's platform on the REFSMMAT the LM's platform was aligned to after the incident (the Apollo Flight Journal: the passive thermal control REFSMMAT), on which the LM's DPS burns were flown: from their ΔV in the IMU's axes (the Mission Operations Report's, as planned: the free return's -37.89, +2.96, -1.21 and PC+2's +743.08, -426.42, +90.84 ft/s) and in the report's mean equator and equinox of B1970.0 (MSC-02680, Table 6.4-I, desired: +2.9, -34.3, -16.2 and -426.4, +645.6, +379.0 ft/s, whose signs run against the burns) [published], put in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived: the two burns 154.3 deg apart in both; the platform's Z axis within 0.06 deg of the ecliptic's south pole and its Y axis against the equinox, a passive thermal control REFSMMAT's form]. The stack at the attitude the CM's gimbal angles gave for the docked coarse align, 355.57, 167.78 and 351.87 deg (Apollo Flight Journal, 058:04:03) [published; simplified: held from the start, the incident's venting not flown]. The cryogenic tanks as they were at the incident: oxygen 255.0 and 242.0 lb, hydrogen 21.9 and 22.3 lb, in tanks 1 and 2 (MSC-02680, section 7.1.3) [published]

lifeboat._comment: The LGC's platform after the docked alignment: the CMC's REFSMMAT, misaligned as the guidance supplement found it at PC+2 from that burn's error, -0.062, -0.035 and +0.344 deg about the IMU's axes, 0.351 deg (the velocity check; the Sun check gave 0.51 deg, the gyro drift check 0.60 deg) [published]: angles that turn the platform back onto the REFSMMAT, found from the burn's residual, the velocity still to be gained (its 5.27 ft/s across the burn took the return's vacuum perigee to 80.6 nmi, MSC-02680, Table 4-III), and taken whole at the docked alignment [simplified: it grew with the gyros' drift until PC+2]: _refsmmat_pad()

free_return._comment: The midcourse correction that put the stack back on a free return, on the docked LM's descent engine: the PAD's TIG, 61:29:42.84, and N81 -21.3, +4.1, -31.2 ft/s, from which the RTCC starts its solve (Apollo Flight Journal, 060:53:09) [published]; flown 37.8 ft/s in 34.2 s, past the Moon 136 nmi up at 77:20:57, 3.02 N 179.29 W (MSC-02680, Table 4-III) [published], and home to a landing in the Indian Ocean at 152:02:00 (Apollo Flight Journal, 076:32:57) [published]. The report's state at its cutoff (ibid., Table 4-II, its heading read 116.54 deg: at the report's pericynthion), put in the simulator, returns inclined return_inclination_deg to the equator [derived]; entry interface at ei_get, the landing's time less the 13 min 55 s the flown entry took [derived], in the corridor tei's entry_perigee_alt_km [simplified: the ground left the free return's own perigee to a later correction, about 4 ft/s]

tei.name: PC+2
tei._comment: PC+2, two hours past the pericynthion, on the docked LM's descent engine: the final PAD's TIG, 79:27:38.30, and N81 +833.0, -50.9, -213.9 ft/s, from which the RTCC starts its solve, and its throttle, 5 s at the minimum, 21 s at 40 % and the rest at full thrust (Apollo Flight Journal, 077:55:24) [published], the minimum 12.6 % as flown (MSC-02680, section 6.4.2) [published]; flown 860.5 ft/s in 263.8 s from 79:27:38.95 (ibid., Table 6.4-I). Entry interface came at 142:40:45.7, 28.23 S 173.44 E, 36,210.6 ft/s, 6.269 deg down, heading 77.210 deg east of north (ibid., Table 4-II) [published]. That state, put in the simulator, is on a return inclined return_inclination_deg to the equator with its vacuum perigee entry_perigee_alt_km up (Rtcc.vacuum_perigee()) [derived]: the corridor PC+2 and the transearth corrections aim at

entry._comment: Apollo 13's target, N61 in the final entry PAD at 141:48:23 (Apollo Flight Journal): 21.66 deg S, 165.37 deg W [published]. The ground uplinks it with the entry PAD (the timeline's entry_pad)

dispersions._comment: The seed the flight's dispersions are drawn from: the CSM's unmodelled forces (spacecraft.json "unmodelled"), once for the flight, MSFN's tracking error ("msfn"), for each uplink, and the IMUs' coarse aligns

msfn._comment: The Manned Space Flight Network's tracking error in the state vector the RTCC plans the PADs from and uplinks with them (P27): standard deviations in LVLH (X along track, Y right, Z down), by the body the vehicle's orbit is about, Apollo 11's [estimated]

timeline._comment: Mission Control from TLI to the entry. Each entry happens once: at its GET ('get'), or 's' seconds 'after' a mission event or a planned time, or 'before' a planned time (the sequencer's plan), if its condition ('when', a flight phase or one of the sequencer's) holds then; CAPCOM makes the call ('say') and the ground uplinks the PAD ('pad'): the RTCC's solution, a midcourse correction's at its TIG ('tig'), TEI's (PC+2's) at its own. In the lifeboat (the condition 'lifeboat': the LM docked and powered, the CSM's power off) the ground's burns are the docked LM's: on the DPS, with the PAD's throttle schedule ('throttle'), or the LM's jets for a correction under 'rcs_below_ft_s', uplinked to the LGC with the stack's state vector, or read up by voice while the LGC is dark; a midcourse correction marked 'free_return' puts the stack back on a free return (mission.json "free_return"); a transearth correction with a 'tolerance_km' is flown when the vacuum perigee is off the corridor by more than that [estimated: MCC-7's 3 ft/s took 0.25 deg off the entry's angle, some 6 km of perigee]; the ground's coarse align angles ('coarse') and REFSMMAT ('refsmmat') are for the computer the entry names ('computer'), the REFSMMAT after a docked alignment ('docked', _refsmmat_pad()). The times, calls and PADs are Apollo 13's [published: the Apollo Flight Journal: GO for TLI 1:48:11; the MCC-2 PAD 028:49:06, TIG 030:40:49.00; GO for MCC-2 029:30:27; the emergency power-down 056:16:08; to the LM 057:41:31; the CM's IMU kept up for the LM's coarse align 057:48:17; the CSM's power-down 058:36:40; the LM's fine align torquing 058:44:24, its REFSMMAT uplinked by 059:28:03; the free return's PAD 060:53:09, TIG 061:29:42.84, 5 s at the minimum and the rest at 40 % (flown at 12.7 %, MSC-02680, section 6.4.2); GO for it 061:28:53; the final PC+2 PAD 077:55:24; GO for PC+2 079:18:15; the PGNS powered down 082:03:27; the MCC-5 PAD 104:33:43, TIG 105:30:00.00 at 10 %; the Sun and Moon P52 from 134:39:32, torqued 135:04:25; the MCC-7 PAD 136:05:46, TIG 137:39:48.39, 3.1 ft/s on the LM's jets (MCC-7 was to be on the jets since 132:39:01); the SM SEP PAD 136:09:06; the CM's coarse align angles 139:51:40; GO for the CM's power-up 140:09:52; its state vector 140:24:29; the REFSMMAT flag 140:44:55; GO for LM JETT 141:17:49; the farewell 141:30:05, 9 s after the jettison; the final entry PAD 141:48:23; the final state vector 142:00:45]. The ground's coarse align angles and REFSMMATs are the local vertical frame at their time (Imu.nominal()) [simplified: the LGC's for MCC-7 and the CM's entry REFSMMAT]: the LGC's in place of its Sun and Moon P52, the CM's for its coarse align and its star P52 (140:52). The REFSMMAT uplinks come with their flags set, after the crew's coarse aligns [simplified]

entries.say: Okay, Jim. The computer is yours. And you are Go for TLI.
13, Houston. You're Go for MCC-2. Everything's looking good here.
13, Houston. Go to your G&C checklist, the pink pages, 1-5. Do powerdown until we get a Delta of 10 amps.
Odyssey, Houston. We'd like you to start making your way over to the LM now.
Odyssey, Houston. We're going to keep the IMU up so as we can get a coarse align in the LM.
Odyssey, Houston. Close the reactants valve on fuel cell 2. Power down your inverters. Power down your battery relay bus. Battery ties, off, and pull your entry battery circuit breakers.
Aquarius, Houston. You're Go for the burn.
Aquarius, Houston. Jim, you are Go for the burn.
Aquarius, Houston. We're going to open the IMU Operate circuit breaker; close and leave closed the IMU Standby circuit breaker, so we can have heaters.
Aquarius, Houston. We'd like to start charging the command module's entry batteries from the LM.
entries._estimated: the time, the mission report's 'approximately 112 hours' (MSC-02680, section 7.2.5), and the words, the simulator's own: the Flight Journal's pages from 106 to 131 hours aren't in hand

entries.say: Aquarius, Houston. At 138:10:00, which is EI minus 4.5 hours, execute a push of 0.5 feet per second, four jet, plus-X; perform SM Sep; then execute pull, 0.5 feet per second, four jet, minus-X.
Odyssey, Houston. You're Go to start powering up the Command Module.
Odyssey, Houston. We just had a formal Go for LM Jett at your convenience.
Farewell, Aquarius, and we thank you.

failures._comment: Cryogenic oxygen tank 2 failed at 55:54:53 (MSC-02680, Table 3-I) [published]: the failure catalog's o2_tank_2 (data/failures.json)

Pogo shut the S-II's centre engine down at 330.65 s (MPR-SAT-FE-70-2, Table 2-2, and section 8.2.3.2) [published]: the failure catalog's s2_engine_5, armed on the holddown arms' release at 0.3 s so that only the launch start flies it
